props.title: Scary Movie
props.initialSlug: Horror spoof turns slasher clichés into laughs

sections.content: Scary Movie marked a pivotal shift in horror-comedy, aggressively parodying the slasher revival led by Scream (1996) and I Know What You Did Last Summer (1997). The Wayans Brothers cranked up the raunch factor and slapstick violence, moving beyond subtle satire into outrageous spoof territory. While Airplane! (1980) and The Naked Gun (1988) established the spoof template, Scary Movie's crude humor and direct scene-for-scene parodies created a new blueprint that dominated comedy throughout the 2000s.

sections.content: The massive success of Scary Movie spawned an avalanche of increasingly desperate parody films. Date Movie (2006), Epic Movie (2007), and Disaster Movie (2008) copied the formula but missed the sharp pop culture commentary. Only Shaun of the Dead (2004) and Tucker & Dale vs Evil (2010) managed to elevate beyond mere mockery into genuine genre celebration.

The film's impact extended beyond comedy. Scream 4 (2011) directly referenced Scary Movie's meta-commentary, while horror comedies like The Final Girls (2015) balanced genuine scares with self-aware humor. The trend of horror-comedy hybridization continues with films like The Babysitter (2017) and Happy Death Day (2017) maintaining that delicate balance between scares and laughs. SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Horror Parody

movies.title: Tucker & Dale vs Evil
movies.slug: Clever horror-comedy that flips slasher tropes by making the hillbillies the good guys

sections.content: While Young Frankenstein (1974) and Student Bodies (1981) pioneered horror-comedy, Scary Movie's influence pushed the genre into more extreme territory. Modern entries like Cabin in the Woods (2011) and What We Do in the Shadows (2014) demonstrate how horror parody has matured, combining genuine frights with intelligent humor rather than relying solely on crude gags and reference jokes.
